articles.title: Qualcomm Wants Out of Your Pocket and Into the Data Center. The Bet Is on AI Inference.
articles.excerpt: The chipmaker that put Snapdragon in nearly every Android phone is now chasing a $35 billion data-center market by 2031 — and Indian engineers across its design and India teams are central to the pivot.
articles.image_caption: Rows of servers in a data center, the market Qualcomm is now targeting with AI inference chips
articles.nri_angle: Qualcomm's pivot into AI data-center silicon reshapes the career map for thousands of Indian-origin chip designers in San Diego and Hyderabad — and signals where the next wave of semiconductor hiring will land.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Private Orbital Rocket Just Cleared Its Biggest Engine Test. Skyroot's Launch Window Is Open.
articles.excerpt: A successful KALAM-1200 motor test puts Hyderabad's Skyroot Aerospace — now India's first space-tech unicorn — on the final approach to a maiden Vikram-1 flight that could rewrite who launches satellites for the world.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh, India's first private rocket launch
articles.nri_angle: A private Indian company launching its own orbital rocket is a credibility marker NRIs have waited a generation for — and a live investment thesis as global funds like GIC and BlackRock pile into India's space sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Salesforce Just Paid $3.6 Billion to Buy the Robot That Answers Your Support Tickets
articles.excerpt: The acquisition of Fin — formerly Intercom — supercharges Benioff's Agentforce push and accelerates a shift that lands hardest on the Indian BPO and customer-support workforce.
articles.image_caption: Salesforce Tower in San Francisco, headquarters of the CRM giant now betting heavily on AI agents
articles.nri_angle: Salesforce's bet on autonomous customer-service agents threatens the millions of Indian jobs built on call centers and IT support — even as it expands the AI engineering roles Indian talent is racing to fill.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HCLTech Just Bet $151 Million on Sarvam AI. India's IT Giants Are Done Renting Their Intelligence.
articles.excerpt: The Noida outsourcing giant is leading Sarvam's Series B and taking a 10.5% stake, a sign that India's IT services model is pivoting from selling labor to owning models.
articles.image_caption: TheStevieAwards via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: For the hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers at HCLTech, Infosys, and Wipro client sites across the US, the shift from staffing seats to owning AI models redraws what an IT-services career will look like over the next decade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adani and an Apple Supplier Are Building India's AI Data-Center Factory. The Hyperscalers Are the Customers.
articles.excerpt: Jabil, which already builds parts for Apple, is teaming with Adani to manufacture AI and data-center hardware in India, part of a planned $50 billion buildout of the country's digital backbone.
articles.image_caption: Gautam Adani, whose group is partnering with an Apple supplier to build AI data-center capacity in India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs weighing Adani-linked stocks and India's data-center boom now have a concrete signal that the country wants to manufacture AI infrastructure, not just consume it, with implications for cross-border investment and the engineers who will run it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Startup Raised $30 Million to Answer the Calls You Don't Want. NRIs With Indian Numbers Know the Pain.
articles.excerpt: Equal AI's call-screening app is built for the spam-call avalanche of Indian phone numbers, including the code-mixed Hinglish that trips up Western voice models.
articles.image_caption: The Bengaluru startup is building AI to screen the spam and scam calls that flood Indian phone numbers
articles.nri_angle: Any NRI who still keeps an Indian SIM for banking, family, or UPI knows the relentless spam-call problem; Equal AI is building voice models for exactly the multilingual, code-mixed reality the diaspora lives in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Sent 44,000 Crypto Tax Notices and Found $104 Million Hidden. NRIs With Wallets Back Home Should Read the Fine Print.
articles.excerpt: A data-matching crackdown is reconciling exchange records against tax filings — and dual-status investors are squarely in its path.
articles.image_caption: Bitcoin tokens, representing cryptocurrency holdings under tax scrutiny in India
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who hold or trade crypto on Indian exchanges face a 30% flat tax, 1% TDS, and now algorithmic data-matching that flags undisclosed gains — making record-keeping a compliance necessity, not an afterthought.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Uber and Lyft Are Suing New York Over a Law That Stops Them Firing Drivers Quickly. Indian Immigrant Drivers Are Watching Closely.
articles.excerpt: Local Law 52 would bar 'wrongful deactivations' — and for the South Asian drivers who fill these fleets, a sudden app ban can mean losing a livelihood overnight.
articles.image_caption: A rideshare driver uses a smartphone navigation app inside a car at night
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of South Asian immigrants drive for Uber and Lyft in U.S. cities; a law limiting arbitrary 'deactivations' directly affects their job security, while the platforms argue it forces them to keep unsafe drivers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Funding Its Own Eyes in the Sky. A Bengaluru Startup Just Won a Grant to Build AI That Sees the Subcontinent.
articles.excerpt: SatSure's $2.6 million award is a small cheque with a big idea behind it: sovereign Earth-observation models trained on India's own land, not borrowed from the West.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: India's push for sovereign space-AI infrastructure opens cross-border investment and engineering opportunities for NRIs in deep tech, while reducing the country's dependence on foreign satellite-data providers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Tech Back Office Is Now the Brain. Its Workforce Is About to Cross 2.36 Million.
articles.excerpt: A US cybersecurity firm just opened a Bengaluru capability center and pledged to grow it 50% in six months. The reason was not cost — it was talent the company could not find anywhere else.
articles.image_caption: A technology park in Bengaluru, the hub of India's global capability center boom
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing a return to India, the global capability center boom now offers headquarters-grade work — product, R&D, and AI engineering — at home rather than a back-office demotion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bay Area Tech Layoffs Hit 9,284 — Already Worse Than All of Last Year. For H-1B Workers, the Clock Starts Ticking.
articles.excerpt: Fresh WARN filings push 2026's regional job cuts past the entire first half of 2025, with six months still to run. For visa holders, a layoff opens a 60-day countdown that most American colleagues never have to think about.
articles.image_caption: Office workstations in a Silicon Valley technology company
articles.nri_angle: A pink slip means a 60-day grace period to find a new sponsor or leave the country — a deadline that turns every layoff round into an immigration emergency for thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B and L-1 visas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: $1.3 Trillion Vanished From AI Chip Stocks in a Week. Then They Had Their Best Day in a Year.
articles.excerpt: A single cautious sentence from Broadcom triggered one of the sharpest semiconductor selloffs in years — and a violent rebound days later. For Indian-American investors and tech workers paid in stock, the whiplash is the new normal.
articles.image_caption: A close-up of a semiconductor wafer used in advanced AI chips
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American households are heavily concentrated in tech equities and equity compensation — RSUs, ESPPs, and chip-heavy index funds — so a $1.3 trillion swing in AI semiconductors lands directly on diaspora net worth, not just on Wall Street screens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sriram Krishnan Wrote America's AI Playbook. Now He's Leaving the White House to Build His Own.
articles.excerpt: The Chennai-born policy adviser shaped the AI Action Plan, brokered government access to frontier models, and navigated the Anthropic crisis. His next move is a startup.
articles.image_caption: Sriram Krishnan, former White House senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence
articles.nri_angle: The most senior Indian-American in US AI policy is leaving at a moment when AI export controls directly threaten Indian IT firms and the 300,000 Indian-origin professionals in American tech.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Launching 16 Electric Vehicles in Nine Months. For Every New Petrol Car, Two EVs Are Pulling Up.
articles.excerpt: Starting this week, Mercedes, Tata, Toyota, BYD, Mahindra, and Maruti are flooding India's market with EVs and plug-in hybrids. The ratio to new ICE models is 2:1.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Tata Motors and Mahindra stand to benefit from India's EV leadership, while the charging infrastructure buildout changes the experience of visiting India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Razorpay Just Filed for a $600 Million IPO. India's Payments War Is About to Go Public.
articles.excerpt: The fintech giant's confidential filing targets a $5–6 billion valuation — well below its 2021 peak — as Indian startups rush to prove they can survive the public markets.
articles.image_caption: The Razorpay logo — the Bengaluru-based payment gateway has filed for a $600 million IPO (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Razorpay processes $180 billion in annual payments including cross-border UPI transactions — making it the invisible plumbing behind every NRI's Swiggy order, Zerodha trade, or Zomato delivery. Its IPO is a litmus test for whether India's fintech boom can deliver public-market returns to diaspora investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zoho Built Its Own Server in Nagpur. It Took Five Years and a Mountain Pass's Name.
articles.excerpt: The 'Nathu La' platform — designed entirely in India on Intel Xeon 6 chips — cuts power consumption by 18% and ownership costs by 30%, marking Zoho's entry into the sovereign hardware race.
articles.image_caption: Sridhar Vembu, founder and CEO of Zoho Corporation, which built its Nathu La server platform in Nagpur (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Zoho serves 100 million users worldwide, including tens of thousands of Indian-origin small business owners in the US. Its move into India-designed hardware signals that Indian tech sovereignty is no longer just a government talking point — it's being built by private companies, with IP owned entirely in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'AI Deflation' Is Squeezing India's IT Giants. Their Own Employees See It First.
articles.excerpt: HCLTech warns of a 3-5% revenue hit. TCS has shed 23,000 workers. Infosys is down 35% from its peak. The $315 billion Indian IT sector is learning what it means to be disrupted by the technology it sells.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bengaluru — India's IT services giants face margin pressure as AI automates traditional outsourcing work (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of NRIs work at or have family in India's big IT firms — and the stocks are staples in Indian household portfolios. AI deflation threatens both careers and savings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American Cybersecurity Giants Are Racing to Arm India's 75 Million Small Businesses
articles.excerpt: As AI-powered attacks surge post-Claude Mythos, Palo Alto Networks and Microsoft are pitching cut-rate security to Indian MSMEs — a market that accounts for nearly a third of India's GDP.
articles.image_caption: Palo Alto Networks headquarters — American cybersecurity firms are expanding rapidly into India's small business market (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs invest in or run family businesses in India. The $3.4 billion cybersecurity surge affects both their portfolio picks (PANW, MSFT) and the family firms back home increasingly under AI-driven attack.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satya Nadella Wants to Kill the App. Project Solara Is How.
articles.excerpt: Microsoft's Build 2026 flagship isn't a new Office feature or a Copilot upgrade. It's an entire operating system — built on Android, not Windows — where AI agents replace apps entirely.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella at a company event
articles.nri_angle: Satya Nadella continues to define the AI-first era from the CEO chair. For the tens of thousands of Indian engineers at Microsoft and its partner ecosystem, Solara signals a fundamental shift in what they'll be building.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asha Sharma's 100-Day Verdict on Xbox: 'This Cannot Continue'
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin CEO's reset memo reveals a gaming division bleeding money at 3% margins, a hardware crisis that has quintupled component costs, and a parent company that hasn't ruled out selling the whole thing.
articles.image_caption: Asha Sharma, who became Xbox president and COO in March 2025 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin executive now holds the reins of one of gaming's most consequential turnarounds — and her decisions will ripple through thousands of Indian engineers at Microsoft's global workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sundar Pichai Is Selling $85 Billion of Alphabet to Win the AI Race. Investors Are Divided.
articles.excerpt: The largest equity offering in tech history includes a $10 billion anchor from Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway. Alphabet plans to spend up to $190 billion this year alone — and it ordered three million TPUs from Intel.
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google
articles.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai's most consequential financial gamble reshapes the company tens of thousands of Indian engineers call home — and it may determine whether Google or OpenAI defines the next era of computing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Just Put 120 Indian Deep-Tech Startups on a Stage in Nice. The Money Is Listening.
articles.excerpt: Bharat Innovates 2026 brings Indian semiconductor, space, and biotech ventures face-to-face with 500 global investors — and it's happening the day before the G7.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who co-inaugurated Bharat Innovates 2026 with French President Macron in Nice
articles.nri_angle: For NRI founders, investors, and professionals debating whether India's deep-tech ecosystem is real, Bharat Innovates is the strongest signal yet that New Delhi is channelling state machinery into turning lab breakthroughs into global businesses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Intel's Stock Has Surged 450% This Year. Lip-Bu Tan's Foundry Gamble Is Starting to Pay Off.
articles.excerpt: Bank of America just double-upgraded Intel to Buy after foundry wins from Google, Microsoft, and potentially Nvidia. The chip giant's most troubled division is becoming its strongest story.
articles.image_caption: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has overseen the company's foundry revival since taking the helm in 2025
articles.nri_angle: Intel's revival directly affects the tens of thousands of Indian engineers who work at the company and across its supply chain — and its American foundry buildout could reshape the H-1B landscape for semiconductor talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NVIDIA Is Hiring 1,200 Foreign Workers While Google and Amazon Cut Theirs in Half
articles.excerpt: As Big Tech slashes H-1B sponsorships amid AI restructuring, Jensen Huang's chipmaker is offering Indian engineers up to $391,000 in base pay — and absorbing a $100,000-per-visa government fee to do it.
articles.image_caption: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang at a company event in 2025
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals hold 71-73% of all H-1B visas — NVIDIA's counter-cyclical hiring expansion is a rare lifeline for thousands of Indian engineers facing layoffs and the 60-day grace period crunch at other tech giants.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Freshworks Cuts 500 Jobs After AI Takes Over Half Its Codebase
articles.excerpt: The Chennai-born SaaS company's revenue is up 16 per cent. Its headcount is down 11 per cent. Welcome to the new math of AI-native software development.
articles.image_caption: TIDEL Park in Chennai, the technology hub where Freshworks was founded before relocating to San Mateo (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Freshworks was the poster child of India's SaaS ambitions — the first Indian-founded company to IPO on the Nasdaq. Its decision to slash 500 jobs because AI writes half the code raises uncomfortable questions about the future of Indian software engineering talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China's $295 Billion AI Grid Bans NVIDIA and AMD. Thousands of Indian Engineers Are Caught in Between.
articles.excerpt: Beijing's five-year data-centre plan mandates 80 per cent domestic technology, squeezing out the US chipmakers where tens of thousands of Indians design the silicon. India's own AI infrastructure spend is a fraction of either rival.
articles.image_caption: ralphrepo via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers at NVIDIA, AMD, and other US chipmakers design the very silicon that China's domestic mandate aims to replace — putting their work at the centre of an escalating superpower tech war while India's own AI infrastructure spend remains a rounding error.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Forbes Names 26 Indian-Origin Immigrants Among America's Most Successful. The List Reads Like a Tech Boardroom.
articles.excerpt: From Vinod Khosla at No. 14 to Padma Lakshmi, Indian-born Americans dominate Forbes' 250th anniversary ranking of the nation's most impactful immigrants.
articles.image_caption: Vinod Khosla at SXSW 2024, the highest-ranked Indian-origin leader on the Forbes list at No. 14
articles.nri_angle: 26 Indian-origin leaders on America's top immigrants list is a data point in the H-1B and immigration debate — and a measure of how deeply the diaspora has shaped the US tech economy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adobe's Next CEO Could Be Indian-Origin Too. Two Candidates Are Already in the Ring.
articles.excerpt: David Wadhwani and Anil Chakravarthy — both Indian-born, both presidents of Adobe's main business units — lead the internal race to succeed Shantanu Narayen.
articles.image_caption: Shantanu Narayen, Adobe's outgoing CEO after an 18-year tenure
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin CEO succeeded by another at a $82B software giant would be unprecedented continuity — and signals the depth of Indian-origin leadership in US tech.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX's Record $75 Billion IPO Lands at $1.75 Trillion. India Just Froze Starlink.
articles.excerpt: Indian retail investors are rushing to buy on platforms like Vested and Borderless, even as New Delhi blocks Starlink's commercial launch over security concerns tied to the Iran conflict.
articles.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches — the company's IPO values it at $1.75 trillion while India freezes Starlink operations
articles.nri_angle: Indian retail investors are pouring money into SpaceX through LRS-enabled platforms, but Starlink's India freeze raises questions about connectivity for NRI families and sovereign tech control.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's IT Stocks Have Lost 27% This Year. BlackRock Says the Market Has It Wrong.
articles.excerpt: Foreign investors have pulled a record $30 billion from Indian equities, but the world's largest asset manager and Lighthouse Canton argue India's 'absence' from the AI trade is being mispriced.
articles.image_caption: India's IT sector — stocks including TCS, Infosys, and Wipro have lost 27% this year, but BlackRock sees opportunity
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors holding TCS, Infosys, or Wipro are watching portfolios bleed — but BlackRock and Lighthouse Canton say the picks-and-shovels AI infrastructure play makes India a contrarian buy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic's Ban Lit a Fire Under India's Sovereign AI Movement. Here's Who's Fanning It.
articles.excerpt: Zoho's Vembu calls globalization dead. Mohandas Pai demands a ₹500 billion AI fund. And TCS just partnered with the very company whose models got pulled.
articles.image_caption: India's technology leaders are pushing for sovereign AI development after Anthropic's suspension of access to its models
articles.nri_angle: H-1B holders building with Claude may soon need to prove citizenship to access frontier models. India's sovereign AI push is no longer academic — it's a professional and national security reality for NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jayshree Ullal's Arista Launches 1.6-Terabit Switches. AI's Bandwidth Bottleneck Just Got an Upgrade.
articles.excerpt: The 7060XE7 Series delivers 100 terabits per second of switching capacity, backed by Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle — and Ullal is positioning Arista at the dead centre of the AI infrastructure buildout.
articles.image_caption: Jayshree Ullal, CEO of Arista Networks
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEO Jayshree Ullal leads the company building the networking backbone for every major AI data centre — a story of diaspora leadership in the invisible layer that makes AI work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nikesh Arora's Palo Alto Networks Posts $3 Billion Quarter. Goldman Says the Real AI Security Boom Hasn't Started.
articles.excerpt: Revenue up 31 per cent, next-gen security ARR surging 60 per cent — and Goldman Sachs argues the agentic AI era will force enterprise security spending into an inflection that mirrors the cloud security lag of 2015.
articles.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, Chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks
articles.nri_angle: Former Google executive Nikesh Arora has turned Palo Alto Networks into the most valuable pure-play cybersecurity company on earth — a story that matters to every NRI investor tracking the AI spending chain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Chip Factories Start Spending Real Money. ₹31,299 Crore Hits the Shop Floor by FY27.
articles.excerpt: Five companies — including Tata Electronics, Micron, and CG Power — have already deployed ₹15,799 crore in FY26, with another ₹15,500 crore queued for equipment procurement as India's semiconductor mission moves from announcements to assembly lines.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: India's semiconductor buildout is creating a new category of return-to-India career opportunities for NRI chip engineers — and an investment thesis that didn't exist three years ago.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Handed Its Broken AI to an Indian-Origin Engineer. He Rebuilt It With Google's Help.
articles.excerpt: Amar Subramanya, Apple's new VP of AI, orchestrated a Gemini collaboration that produced five foundation models and a Siri overhaul years overdue.
articles.image_caption: Apple Park in Cupertino, California — at WWDC 2026, Apple unveiled Siri AI, a ground-up rebuild led by Indian-origin VP Amar Subramanya in collaboration with Google's Gemini team (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin VP of AI Amar Subramanya now controls Apple's most consequential AI deployment, following a career at Google and Microsoft — a trajectory that mirrors hundreds of thousands of Indian technologists in the Valley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Musk's $55 Billion Chip Factory Courts ASML. Indian Engineers Are the Talent It Needs.
articles.excerpt: Terafab's plan for 2-nanometre chips requires thousands of process engineers the US cannot produce domestically. India's semiconductor workforce is watching.
articles.image_caption: ASML headquarters in Veldhoven, Netherlands — the company holds a global monopoly on EUV lithography machines essential for advanced chipmaking
articles.nri_angle: Terafab would compete with India's Dholera and Gujarat fabs for the same Indian-origin semiconductor talent, adding a third option for NRI engineers weighing career moves between the US and India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GitHub Is Drowning in AI-Generated Code. India's 15 Million Developers Feel It First.
articles.excerpt: Nine outages in May, a 30x capacity crunch, and Copilot bills that can hit $750 a month — GitHub's AI bet is straining the platform Indian developers cannot leave.
articles.image_caption: Contributors of github/docs via wikimedia (BY)
articles.nri_angle: India is GitHub's second-largest market with 15 million developers. Outages during US evenings hit Indian working hours, and Copilot's metered pricing disproportionately affects Indian IT shops with tight per-seat budgets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Wrote Its First Cheques to Private Space Startups. The Sector Will Never Be the Same.
articles.excerpt: IN-SPACe has funded three companies building reusable rocket engines, AI-powered earth observation, and satellite navigation systems — the first direct government investment in India's private space sector.
articles.image_caption: A rocket launch from ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors and VCs are watching India's $44-billion-by-2033 space economy take shape, with Skyroot already at unicorn status backed by early Google investor Ram Shriram and BlackRock.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Is Arming 50,000 Workers With Claude. The Company Threatening Its Business Is Now Its Partner.
articles.excerpt: Tata Consultancy Services has become Anthropic's Global Premier Partner, rolling out Claude AI to tens of thousands of employees — even as the technology sends IT stocks to multi-year lows.
articles.image_caption: TCS Chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran at the India Economic Summit
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT professionals on H-1B visas at TCS, Infosys, and Wipro face an uncomfortable question as their employers partner with the very AI companies investors believe will disrupt the $315-billion IT services sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: State Attorneys General Hit OpenAI With a Sweeping Subpoena. The IPO Just Got Harder.
articles.excerpt: A coalition led by New York's AG is demanding documents on data handling, advertising, model sycophancy, and risks to minors — days after OpenAI filed for a trillion-dollar public listing.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman at a meeting in Washington, February 2025
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin executives hold several of OpenAI's top engineering roles, and Indian AI startups are watching the regulatory fallout closely as they build on OpenAI's APIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Broadcom, Apollo, and Blackstone Just Built a $35 Billion Machine to Feed AI's Appetite for Chips
articles.excerpt: The AI XPV Platform will deploy 20 gigawatts of custom compute for Anthropic and OpenAI through 2028. It is the largest private credit deal in AI history.
articles.image_caption: Server racks in an AI data centre — the kind of infrastructure Broadcom is now financing at gigawatt scale
articles.nri_angle: Broadcom is one of the largest H-1B employers in the U.S. with thousands of Indian engineers designing the custom AI accelerators at the centre of this deal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NVIDIA Is Training an AI to Listen to Your Doctor. An Indian-Origin Founder Built the Ears.
articles.excerpt: Dr. Shiv Rao's Abridge is partnering with NVIDIA to build a clinical conversation model trained on real doctor-patient exchanges at 100 health systems, including Kaiser Permanente and Mayo Clinic.
articles.image_caption: A healthcare professional consults with a patient using a digital tablet at a clinic
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin physicians are one of the largest groups of foreign-born doctors in the U.S. — a healthcare AI model built on real clinical data could reshape how over 100,000 Indian American doctors document and deliver care.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Opendoor Just Shut Its Entire India Operation. It Replaced 250 Workers With AI.
articles.excerpt: The US real estate firm's decision to close offices in Chennai, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru is being called a watershed moment for AI-driven outsourcing — and a warning shot for India's $315 billion IT sector.
articles.image_caption: michellehurwitz via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with family in India's IT sector are watching AI compress the cost-arbitrage model that built the H-1B pipeline and offshore development centres.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zepto Wants $837 Million From Public Markets. It Has Ten Months of Cash Left.
articles.excerpt: The quick-commerce unicorn's updated IPO filing reveals soaring revenue, widening losses, and a marketplace pivot it has barely tested — all while India's kirana lobby demands regulators block the listing.
articles.image_caption: A smartphone displays a grocery delivery app surrounded by fresh produce
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Indian tech IPOs get a stress test for the quick-commerce thesis — and a front-row seat to the most politically charged listing of 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NVIDIA's First PC Chip Has Arrived. It Runs a 120-Billion-Parameter AI Model Without the Cloud.
articles.excerpt: RTX Spark, unveiled at Computex 2026, is Jensen Huang's ARM-based bet that a petaflop of local AI compute can lure developers away from MacBooks and reshape the PC market.
articles.image_caption: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, who unveiled the RTX Spark chip at Computex 2026 in Taipei
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers at MediaTek are building the silicon, and the death of cloud-inference costs could unlock local AI for India's startup ecosystem — if the price comes down.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: KPMG Pulled Its Own AI Report After It Turned Out to Be Full of Fabrications
articles.excerpt: Only five of 45 citations were accurate. UBS, the NHS, and Swiss railways all denied the claims made about them. Welcome to 'vibe citing.'
articles.image_caption: KPMG has withdrawn its agentic AI report pending investigation
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indians work at Big Four firms and IT consultancies now deploying AI in client work — this scandal is a warning about what happens when oversight fails.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DRAM Prices Have Doubled This Year. Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron Is Printing Money.
articles.excerpt: The AI boom has created the worst memory chip shortage in a decade. Samsung engineers are getting $400,000 bonuses. Your next laptop will cost more.
articles.image_caption: Sanjay Mehrotra
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin Sanjay Mehrotra runs Micron, one of only three companies that control the global memory supply. His company is building India's first major semiconductor fab in Gujarat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iowa Fires 200 State IT Workers and Hands the Whole Operation to Cognizant
articles.excerpt: The $525 million outsourcing deal sends Iowa's servers to Amazon and its help desk to a New Jersey-based Indian IT giant. Workers got three days to sign up with their replacement.
articles.image_caption: Cognizant Technology Solutions headquarters in Teaneck, New Jersey
articles.nri_angle: Cognizant is one of the largest H-1B sponsors and Indian IT employers in the US — this deal expands Indian IT services into American government infrastructure while fuelling anti-outsourcing sentiment that directly affects NRI tech workers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UPI Now Works in Nine Countries. The Transaction Numbers Are Staggering.
articles.excerpt: A new cross-border corridor with Nepal went live this week. In May alone, India's payment rails processed 23.2 billion transactions worth $358 billion.
articles.image_caption: Mobile phone-based digital money transfer between two devices
articles.nri_angle: UPI's international expansion turns India's payment infrastructure into a global network that NRIs can use abroad — and creates career opportunities for diaspora engineers who understand both Indian and international payment systems.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Cuts Half Its Azure Team in China. The AI Engineers Were Spared.
articles.excerpt: Between 200 and 400 employees in Azure cloud R&D are being eliminated in Beijing and Shanghai. Some were offered relocation to Canada. The AI units were left untouched.
articles.image_caption: Satya Nadella, CEO of Microsoft
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft's India engineering centres are growing while China shrinks — Indian engineers in big tech's AI divisions are well positioned as companies restructure globally around AI.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
